messages:
laura: Heads-up: prepping private installer v2.0.1 (airgap) for late-night delivery to VPC customers. Target window 23:30 UTC. Need final checks on shrinkwrap delta, signer chain, and transport mirroring TTL.

devin: Delta pipeline finished. We produced chunked artifacts (32 chunks). Running final integrity sweep now.

packaging-bot: artifact staged: /staging/offline/v2.0.1/installer.tar.gz (sha256: 9b2f...11c). chunk_count=32.

ryan: Signer migration is in-progress earlier today; current active key is new-kms-2026. We have a fallback policy for legacy signatures for 12h post-delivery.

laura: Important: if we sign with new-kms and any customer mirrors validate only legacy signatures, we will hit validation errors. Option: pin manifest and include both sigs (legacy + new) for compatibility. Thoughts?

cat: Dual-signing is doable but increases package size slightly and requires deploybot to advertise signature versions in the manifest. Ops prefers manifest pinned with both sigs for a rolling validator upgrade.

signer-bot: dual-sign request accepted. will attach signatures: key:new-kms-2026 sig-id:nk-2026-01 and key:legacy-2024 sig-id:lg-2024-17.

laura: Great. Also need rollback policy decided: if canary fails to apply due to checksum mismatch -> immediate auto-rollback to v2.0.0. If canary nodes fail with non-deterministic errors (OOM, kernel panic) -> pause rollout and escalate.

devin: Agreed. Add network fetch retries: 3 attempts with exponential backoff (2s, 6s, 18s). If fetch fails after retries -> mark chunk as suspect and abort canary.

ryan: For transport TTL: set mirror-index TTL=3h for this delivery. That gives ops time to re-ingest if something goes wrong.

packaging-bot: cosign completed. signatures: [nk-2026-01, lg-2024-17]. manifest published: /staging/offline/v2.0.1/manifest.json (manifest_sha: f1c2...8aa). pinned=true.

deploy-bot: deploy job scheduled: private/vpc/offline/v2.0.1 - canary=2 - window=2026-03-21T23:30Z - job_id=9912. monitor: https://deploy.redwood.com/jobs/9912

cat: Quick preflight (local):
```
./scripts/offline_smoke.sh --manifest /staging/offline/v2.0.1/manifest.json --validate-signatures
```
preflight: signatures valid, chunk index mapping OK.

laura: Thanks. Two operational notes: 1) Add a changelog blurb about dual-signatures and validator compatibility. 2) Include instructions for customers on how to verify both signatures via cosign.

devin: Noted. I'll drop the snippet into release notes.

deploy-bot: canary started on hosts worker-pvt-11 and worker-pvt-12. logs: https://logs.redwood.com/9912/hosts

ryan: worker-pvt-11 failed healthcheck after install step with "service failed to start: permission denied". Investigating.

laura: If it's a permission error that's likely a packaging manifest entry mistake. Abort canary and mark rollout paused. We'll open a packaging-hotfix and republish v2.0.1+fix.

devin: I'll start a quick triage. If we need to republish, can we do a delta patch that only updates the offending manifest entry?

cat: Yes, delta patch possible. But customers with strict manifest pinning will need to pull the new manifest hash. We'll coordinate mirror invalidation.

packaging-bot: worker-pvt-11 logs: /staging/logs/9912/worker-pvt-11.log -> shows file mode 0600 on /opt/redwood/bin/start.sh. suspected artifact mode set during packaging.

laura: Ok that's a clear packaging bug. Aborting canary per policy. Deploy job paused. deploy-bot: please mark job 9912 state=paused and preserve artifacts for hotfix branch.

deploy-bot: job 9912 paused by policy (reason: packaging permission error). preserving artifacts at /staging/offline/v2.0.1/hold.

laura: I'll create the packaging-hotfix branch and ping the release manager. We plan to cut v2.0.1.1 with a fix for file modes, retest smoke, re-cosign, and redeploy in next 2-hour window.

devin: Working on a quick fix patch now. ETA 35m for rebuild and preflight.

ryan: FYI: because manifest was pinned, legacy validators won't reject the republish if we keep same manifest path but new SHA. We should mark older manifest as superseded in release notes.

cat: I'll draft a customer notice about the pause and expected timeline: "We've paused the delivery due to a packaging permission issue discovered during canary. We'll republish a patch within ~1 hour and re-run canary. No data loss expected."

laura: Thanks everyone. Keep thread updated. I'll file follow-up incident if hotfix timeline slips past 90m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
